title: Cost quietude: probabilistic prefill sentinel and quantile snapshotter
author: Riley Chen
description: Motivation: On multi-tenant workloads we observe frequent low-value prefill traffic that inflates token cost without improving cache hit-rate. This PR introduces a production-safe "quietude" prefill sentinel: a probabilistic prefill throttle plus a lightweight quantile snapshotter that records prefill size/latency distributions and unit-econ deltas. The goal is automated, low-risk dialing of prefill volume per-tenant and per-model so the platform reduces wasted GPU cycles while preserving cache quality and latency SLOs. What changed (high level): 1) runtime/prefill: add probabilistic prefill sampler and in-memory token budget window; 2) metrics/telemetry: quantile snapshotter that emits p50/p90/p99 prefill size and benefit estimates to telemetry and tenant audit logs; 3) control-plane: new tenant-level config default (quietude mode) + CLI to export snapshots for unit-econ analysis; 4) helm chart and installer: opt-in defaults for Private/Dedicated to enable quietude by default in cost-sensitive tiers. Safety and rollout: defaults are conservative (3% sample start), can be ramped per-tenant with a canary policy. The prefill sampler is decay-based and favors requests with recent positive cache delta signals. Tests: unit + integration + perf harness with synthetic trace replay were added. Related: ENG-8123 (prefill noise reduction), PM-451 (cost exposure UX). Checklist: - [x] prototype runtime sampler - [x] snapshot telemetry + console exporter - [x] policy rollouts and canary gating - [x] unit, integration, perf tests - [x] docs and changelog entries Notes: this description includes reasoning and the rollout plan. See changed_files for file-level summary and review_thread for discussion snippets.

review_thread: Samira Patel (2026-02-19): Nice direction. A couple asks: 1) can we bound worst-case latency impact for cold cache paths? 2) ensure audits expose which requests were sampled for post-hoc analysis.

Riley Chen (2026-02-19): Response: sampler only affects prefill paths not on-path generation; we added a bounded budget window and ensure sampler rejects only when budget exceeded — cold cache generation is unaffected. Audit logs include request ids and sampling decision hash.

Owen Brooks (2026-02-20): Requested change: move the heavy snapshot formatting into a separate thread in the exporter to avoid tail-latency on the host. Also ask for a small perf test against a 2ms token generation baseline.

Riley Chen (2026-02-21): Addressed. Moved formatting to background worker and added a perf scenario in replay_prefill_scenarios.py; CI perf check included a threshold that is now part of the PR checks.
Marta Iglesias (2026-02-22): Approve with comment: confirm CLI export respects RBAC and tenant isolation — looks good after CLI patched to call control-plane auth endpoints.

release_notes: Introduce 'quietude' prefill sentinel (probabilistic prefill throttle) and quantile snapshotter. Conservative defaults for Dedicated/Private. Adds telemetry, CLI export, and runbook. Improves platform unit economics by reducing low-value prefill traffic. Backwards-compatible: no changes to on-path generation flows.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: premature throttling could lower cache hit rates and increase overall token use. Mitigations: conservative start_pct (3%), decay-based sampler favors positive delta signals, canary per-tenant rollout, snapshot export for quick rollback and analysis, and automated guardrails that disable quietude if SLO degradation is detected.
testing_notes: Unit tests for sampler heuristics and decay, integration replay against three synthetic tenant traces (high, medium, low prefill noise). Perf harness ensures p99 latency < +5% and cost per 1M requests measured before/after. Added golden snapshots for quantile exporter. Manual verification steps included in runbook.
